tasks.short: Turn drawings, specifications and rates into a defensible cost estimate.

steps.what: Gather current drawings, specifications and scope instructions.
Read specifications and identify scope, exclusions and unresolved requirements.

loop.input: Versioned specifications and scope instructions from the estimate source pack.
loop.output: Draft scope register with source references, exclusions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Validate document versions and references; estimator approves scope interpretation and missing requirements.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per document; unreadable or conflicting sections go to the estimator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements appear in varied prose and cross-references; fixed fields cannot capture them reliably.

steps.what: Measure quantities and infer labour activities using the drawing measurement tool in {OTHER}.
Retrieve material prices, labour rates and relevant historical costs.
Calculate material, labour, equipment and overhead costs in the estimate workbook.
Assess productivity, uncertainty, exclusions and contingency; document the estimate basis.
Review assumptions and approve the estimate for bidding or pricing.

tasks.design: Configure versioned source packs in {DOCS} and an estimate template in {SPREADSHEET}, with rate retrieval from {ERP} through {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop drafts the scope register with source references; the estimator checks scope, measures quantities and sets uncertainty allowances before commercial approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawing interpretation, inconsistent scope descriptions and disconnected rate sources made end-to-end automation unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates and rate interfaces handle calculation; faster coding makes the connecting work cheaper. Bounded text extraction can prepare a source-linked scope draft.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous drawings, buildability, site conditions and productivity assumptions still require expertise. Reliable geometric extraction is outside this initial build.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an omitted activity or unrealistic production assumption before it becomes an expensive commitment.

ambition.what: An early design-options cost comparison using a common scope and rate basis.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling files and repeating calculations towards comparing design options and testing assumptions. Commercial approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Translate estimate ranges into phased project budgets.
reach.learn: Budget phasing, contingency treatment and the distinction between cost estimates and spending authority.

evidence.claim: Versioned inputs, lookup tables and configured formulas can automate estimate assembly and arithmetic.
Scope extraction from specifications is plausible with bounded review; the digest contains no direct estimator deployment evidence.

assumptions: The reference workflow uses construction or engineered-product drawings; service estimates substitute activity volumes for drawing quantities.
The build covers one estimating template family and a limited set of source connections.
Approved rates have units, currencies, dates and applicability rules.
GDPR applies to identifiable labour data; EU AI Act obligations depend on actual use. Access time includes national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Whether drawings contain usable structured quantities or require manual measurement.
Which source identifies the latest authorised drawing revision.
Rate ownership, licensing restrictions and available interfaces.
Existing estimate software capabilities and commercial approval limits.
research_questions: Does existing software already provide rate lookup and estimate generation without custom code?
How accurately can scope extraction find exclusions and cross-references on representative specifications?
new_work: Review extracted scope against source passages.
Resolve stale rates, missing units and conflicting revisions.
Maintain estimate templates, rate mappings and regression examples.
Check generated packs for unsupported assumptions.
tasks.statement: Analyze blueprints and other documentation to prepare time, cost, materials, and labor estimates.

tasks.short: Compare actual costs with bids and judge whether delivery remains cost effective.

steps.what: Retrieve actual costs, commitments and delivery progress against the approved estimate.
Reconcile cost codes, accruals, commitments and scope changes in the monitoring workbook.
Calculate variance, unit costs and forecast scenarios against the bid baseline.
Investigate material variances and challenge progress and remaining-work assumptions.
Assess cost effectiveness and recommend delivery or forecast changes.
Approve corrective actions and the updated forecast within delegated limits.

tasks.design: Use existing variance reporting in {ERP} first, adding deterministic feeds from {PROCUREMENT} and {PROJECT} through {DATA_PLATFORM} where needed. Configure reconciliation checks and a {BI} dashboard that preserves the original bid and approved changes; estimators investigate exceptions and project managers approve forecasts and actions through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, commitments and progress arrived on different schedules and used different structures. Recurring reconciliation consumed time before useful analysis could start.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and dashboard features already cover much of the calculation. Faster integration development makes cross-system refresh and exception routing more affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Actual costs lag delivery, progress can be overstated, and commitments can overlap invoices. Forecast quality still depends on credible remaining-work assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing timing differences from real cost deterioration and selecting an operational response that preserves value.

ambition.what: A weekly remaining-cost intervention decision for active projects with material exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The estimator reviews exceptions throughout the week instead of rebuilding a monthly workbook. They can initiate earlier intervention discussions; spending and forecast approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Translate project cost changes into the rolling forecast.
reach.learn: Forecast drivers, uncertainty ranges and the separation of baseline, forecast and budget.

reach.task: Compare corrective actions by margin and cash impact.
reach.learn: Incremental costs, sunk costs and working-capital effects.

evidence.claim: Structured actual-versus-baseline calculations, exception rules and dashboards generally need deterministic technology.
Cost-to-complete forecasts require judgement about remaining work and cannot be inferred from spending alone.

assumptions: Project identifiers can be mapped across finance, purchasing and delivery records.
The baseline, approved changes and current forecast remain separate.
Forecast scenarios are provisional until approved; alerts do not authorise spending.
GDPR applies where costs identify individuals. EU AI Act duties depend on actual use; national consultation requirements need assessment if monitoring practices change.
unknowns: Whether existing reports already reconcile invoices, accruals and open commitments.
Reliability and frequency of progress updates.
Materiality thresholds, forecast ownership and escalation limits.
Whether labour costs can be supplied at an aggregated level.
research_questions: Which reconciliation failures most often distort the current cost position?
What refresh frequency would enable an operational decision before costs become unavoidable?
new_work: Resolve unmatched costs and commitment overlaps.
Maintain baseline mappings and materiality thresholds.
Check stale progress inputs and failed refreshes.
Review whether alerts produced useful interventions.
tasks.statement: Assess cost effectiveness of products, projects or services, tracking actual costs relative to bids as the project develops.

tasks.short: Discuss scope, costs and uncertainties with stakeholders, resolve disagreements, and agree estimate assumptions.

steps.what: Collect current scope, drawings, quotations and estimate versions.
Read the source pack and prepare questions about gaps and conflicting assumptions.

loop.input: Current consultation source pack with document versions and source references.
loop.output: Questions and conflicting assumptions, each linked to supporting passages.
loop.check: Validate source references; the estimator checks relevance and missing issues.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per pack; unsupported claims become questions for manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Conflicting scope descriptions require reading free text; version checks remain deterministic.

steps.what: Discuss practical constraints, challenge assumptions and resolve stakeholder disagreements.
Approve scope assumptions that affect the project baseline.
Write the consultation record and assign follow-up actions.

loop.input: Written discussion notes and approved scope assumptions.
loop.output: Draft consultation record with decisions, unresolved questions, owners and due dates.
loop.check: Every decision links to an approved assumption; the estimator verifies owners and commitments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous actions remain unassigned for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes express decisions and actions inconsistently.

tasks.design: An integration gathers versioned evidence from {DOCS}, {PROJECT} and {PROCUREMENT}; a bounded loop drafts the agenda with source references. People conduct the discussion and approve changed assumptions, then a second bounded loop prepares the record and actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scope evidence was scattered, and meeting notes rarely followed a consistent structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document access and version controls support source gathering. Bounded text processing can prepare questions and records without taking over the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Site conditions, unstated constraints and stakeholder disagreements require direct questioning. Old drawings and incomplete notes remain expensive to interpret.
tasks.human_edge: The estimator notices hesitation, tests practical feasibility and earns agreement on uncomfortable cost assumptions.

ambition.what: An early scope-risk clinic before the first priced estimate.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling packs and writing minutes; more goes into early scope-risk discussions. Project baseline approval stays with the project manager; no decision rights transfer automatically.

reach.task: Assess exposure from unresolved scope assumptions.
reach.learn: Distinguish likely cost variation from rare losses and define escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Source gathering, agenda drafting and action extraction are feasible support tools; stakeholder agreement remains human.
The documented flawed-report case supports checking generated statements against original sources.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative for a mid-size company, not measured customer results.
The communication-heavy prior fits this task; preparation and records remain separate opportunities.
Written notes are available; recording meetings is outside the proposed design.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one workflow using existing infrastructure.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Consultation under national rules may apply if employee-data use changes.
unknowns: Which role can approve scope changes and external commitments?
Are document versions and project identifiers reliable?
What consultation, retention and access requirements apply to stakeholder notes?
research_questions: Can current document permissions be preserved during source retrieval?
How often do source-linked agendas reveal material issues missed in current preparation?
new_work: Review generated questions and consultation records.
Resolve stale documents and ambiguous action ownership.
Maintain source mappings, access controls and note templates.
tasks.statement: Consult with clients, vendors, personnel in other departments, or construction foremen to discuss and formulate estimates and resolve issues.

tasks.short: Agree estimate changes with technical specialists, customers and delivery partners.

steps.what: Compare the requested change with the approved estimate and prepare discussion points.

loop.input: Change request, approved estimate and estimate basis.
loop.output: Draft change brief with affected scope, source references and open questions.
loop.check: Check estimate version and line references; estimator validates scope interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved scope remains explicitly open.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests describe changes in prose and often imply dependencies absent from standard fields.

steps.what: Arrange the discussion and circulate the approved change brief.
Discuss technical alternatives, challenge assumptions and negotiate acceptable scope adjustments.
Document proposed agreements, unresolved issues and action owners.

loop.input: Estimator's discussion notes and proposed change terms.
loop.output: Draft change log separating proposed agreements, open issues and actions.
loop.check: Estimator checks each commitment, owner and date against notes; uncertain agreements remain unconfirmed.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; disputed wording returns to the participants.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need interpretation to distinguish a proposal from an agreement.

steps.what: Recalculate affected estimate lines and show the cost difference.
Approve the revised estimate within delegated limits or escalate it.

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW} to prepare a source-linked change brief, schedule discussion through {CALENDAR}, and draft a change log from written notes. Keep negotiation with people; configured calculations in {SPREADSHEET} produce a revised estimate for approval in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The core work depends on trust and technical negotiation, while preparation and documentation were scattered across files.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can organise change requests and notes. Existing scheduling, formula and approval features can handle the surrounding administration.
tasks.still_hard: Participants may disagree about scope, liability or what was agreed. A concise draft cannot settle those disputes.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering what each party can accept and recognising when apparent agreement conceals a costly misunderstanding.

ambition.what: A costed alternative-options brief before contentious change discussions.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends less time preparing packs and recording decisions, leaving more preparation time for difficult conversations. Negotiation and approval limits stay unchanged.

reach.task: Assess the margin and cash implications of a proposed scope change.
reach.learn: Margin bridges, payment timing and delegated commercial authority.

evidence.claim: Configured scheduling, estimate formulas and approval routing can automate administration around a human discussion.
Bounded drafting from written notes can reduce documentation work, subject to checking commitments.

assumptions: Scheduling uses an approved participant list and approved brief; it makes no commercial commitment.
Recalculation follows estimator-confirmed quantities and rates; unresolved technical changes return to the estimator.
Approval follows delegated limits; contract amendments need their separate authorised approval.
The build uses written notes without introducing meeting recording.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the actual use; national consultation rules apply where relevant.
unknowns: Who can approve each class and value of change.
Whether external participants can access the shared change brief.
How approved estimate revisions are distinguished from contract variations.
Whether an existing workflow already covers change control.
research_questions: Can structured change forms remove enough ambiguity to avoid a drafting loop for routine requests?
Can reviewers reliably detect draft wording that overstates agreement?
new_work: Check draft briefs and change logs.
Resolve disputed commitments and unclear action owners.
Maintain participant access and approval limits.
Keep estimate revisions linked to the correct change decision.
tasks.statement: Confer with engineers, architects, owners, contractors, and subcontractors on changes and adjustments to cost estimates.

tasks.short: Prepare cost and resource estimates that management uses to plan, organise and schedule work.

steps.what: Collect scope, quantities, actual costs, capacity and the current project schedule.
Clarify work quantities, sequencing constraints and resource availability with the project manager.
Calculate resource quantities, direct costs, overheads and time-phased expenditure.
Choose realistic productivity, contingency and sequencing assumptions.
Recalculate alternative schedules and resource mixes to compare costs and timing.
Prepare the management estimate with assumptions, cost ranges and schedule implications.
Review the estimate and approve the selected cost and resource baseline.

tasks.design: Connect cost, capacity and schedule data from {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PROJECT} to versioned calculation rules on {DATA_PLATFORM}. A small scenario form in {WORKFLOW} recalculates costs and produces a templated management pack in {DOCS}, with comparisons in {BI}. People choose credible assumptions and approve the baseline before it updates {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost codes, schedules and resource plans did not align. Spreadsheet scenarios were easy to copy but difficult to refresh and trace.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared identifiers, explicit formulas and versioned assumptions support repeatable scenarios. AI-assisted coding can make the required forms and connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Productivity, changing scope and feasible sequencing remain judgement calls. A precise calculation can still rest on a weak assumption.
tasks.human_edge: The estimator understands how work actually happens and challenges a schedule that looks affordable but cannot be delivered.

ambition.what: Weekly management decisions on the cost of resequencing constrained work.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends more time testing realistic resource and schedule alternatives and less rebuilding calculation sheets. Management retains baseline approval; no new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Translate project estimates into phased budget forecasts.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, forecast horizons and treatment of committed versus expected expenditure.

reach.task: Compare planning assumptions with realised costs and throughput.
reach.learn: Data lineage, comparable cohorts and separation of scope variance from productivity variance.

evidence.claim: Explicit quantity, rate, overhead and time-phasing rules support deterministic estimate and scenario generation.
Dashboards and versioned records can connect planning estimates with actual costs; the digest supplies no direct estimator implementation case.
Credible productivity and sequencing assumptions still require operational judgement.

assumptions: This is a project-based example; manufacturing and service estimates use equivalent quantity and capacity structures.
Capacity data is aggregated by role or work centre, without individual worker scoring.
The low rule-coverage prior describes assumption choice; established arithmetic still supports deterministic automation.
Existing estimating features should be configured first if they cover the required model.
Time and build ranges are illustrative for one planning model with existing infrastructure.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Changed employee-data use requires assessment of consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which estimating and scenario functions already exist?
Are costs, capacity and schedules linked by reliable identifiers?
Which productivity and overhead assumptions are approved?
Who can approve resource changes and baseline updates?
Does capacity data identify employees, and what access or consultation is required?
research_questions: Can current estimating tools produce traceable, time-phased scenarios without custom calculations?
Which historical projects are comparable enough to validate assumptions?
Which model discrepancies materially change a management decision?
new_work: Maintain approved rate tables, scenario rules and cost-code mappings.
Review data freshness and missing capacity or schedule inputs.
Compare assumptions with actual outcomes and explain material differences.
Manage calculation versions and failed baseline updates.
tasks.statement: Prepare estimates used by management for purposes such as planning, organizing, and scheduling work.

tasks.short: Build comparable supplier and subcontractor cost estimates to support selection and negotiation.

steps.what: Gather quotations, scope requirements and historical cost records.
Read quotations and map inclusions, exclusions and quantities to a common scope.

loop.input: Supplier quotations, approved scope and common work-package schema.
loop.output: Source-linked quotation lines, proposed scope mappings and explicit exclusions.
loop.check: Validate totals, currencies and units; the estimator approves mappings and unresolved scope gaps.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per quotation; ambiguous mappings remain unmatched.
loop.why_not_simpler: Suppliers describe equivalent work differently and bury exclusions in prose; structured quotes bypass the loop.

steps.what: Calculate comparable costs using approved quantities, rates, conversions and cost additions.
Assess delivery risk, exclusions and realistic allowances for incomplete supplier scope.
Assemble the selection estimate with comparisons, allowances, assumptions and source references.
Check material assumptions and approve the estimate for selection discussions.

tasks.design: An integration gathers quotations and historical costs from {PROCUREMENT}, {ERP} and {DOCS}; a bounded extraction loop proposes common scope mappings for review. Deterministic calculations produce comparable costs and a templated selection pack, while people set risk allowances and approve the estimate. The approved estimate links back to the tender record in {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quotes used inconsistent scope descriptions and units. Historical costs lacked reliable links to comparable work packages.
tasks.enabler_now: A common line schema and versioned rate tables make calculations repeatable. Bounded extraction can handle variable quote wording, while AI-assisted coding reduces integration effort.
tasks.still_hard: Missing scope, supplier capability and uncertain future costs cannot be settled by arithmetic. Building a trustworthy work-package history takes effort.
tasks.human_edge: The estimator distinguishes a credible low price from a quote that omits difficult work or transfers risk.

ambition.what: A supplier substitution cost study before final scope commitment.

tasks.altitude: More time goes into challenging exclusions and testing alternative suppliers; less goes into copying quote lines and rebuilding tables. The estimator can recommend alternatives, while supplier award authority remains unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile awarded supplier costs with recorded project actuals.
reach.learn: Cost-code mapping, accrual timing and separation of scope changes from price variance.

reach.task: Assess supplier concentration and delivery exposure.
reach.learn: How concentration and delivery uncertainty affect commercial allowances.

evidence.claim: Common quotation schemas, deterministic cost calculations and templated comparison reports are feasible without autonomous agents.
Transporeon checks freight invoices against contracted rates; this supports rate-based checking as an adjacent pattern, not supplier-estimate automation.
Free-text scope mapping needs source checks and estimator review; the digest supplies no direct cost-estimator case.

assumptions: The example uses project work packages; manufacturing equivalents use parts, routing and service lines.
Calculation rules can be explicit even when scope and risk judgement have low rule coverage.
Structured quotations use direct imports before any model loop.
Time shares and build ranges are illustrative, not promised savings.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National consultation rules may apply if the design changes employee-data use.
unknowns: Which cost additions, tax treatment, currencies and rate sources are approved?
How often are quotation lines already structured?
Are historical actuals comparable after scope changes?
Who approves estimates and supplier awards?
What supplier confidentiality and access restrictions apply?
research_questions: Can existing comparison features handle the required cost model before custom code is built?
Which scope mappings produce the most costly review errors?
Can supplier response schemas remove repeated manual normalisation?
new_work: Review quote mappings, exclusions and unmatched lines.
Maintain units, rate versions, cost additions and work-package mappings.
Reconcile estimate outcomes with actual supplier costs.
Handle missing quotes, failed imports and stale source data.
tasks.statement: Prepare estimates for use in selecting vendors or subcontractors.

tasks.short: Compare internal production costs with supplier offers and recommend whether to make or buy.

steps.what: Review specifications, quantities, quality requirements and delivery dates.
Confirm material needs, labour hours, capacity and feasible production routes.
Request comparable supplier quotations and clarify scope.
Read quotations and identify price breaks, exclusions, tooling charges and delivery terms.

loop.input: Supplier quotes, comparison scope and a fixed quotation-field schema.
loop.output: Quote fields with page references, units, validity dates and unresolved exclusions.
loop.check: Validate required fields, currencies, units and price arithmetic; the estimator approves extracted terms before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per quote; ambiguous or missing terms enter manual clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express exclusions and commercial terms in varying free text. Structured portal fields should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Calculate comparable costs and test demand, utilisation, scrap and delivery scenarios.
Recommend an option, explaining capacity opportunity costs and supply risks.
Approve the make-or-buy decision and its conditions.

tasks.design: A reusable comparison calculator imports approved requirements and rates from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PROCUREMENT}, with validated file imports where direct access is unavailable. A bounded loop extracts unstructured quote terms from the {DOCS}; deterministic calculations produce scenarios, while the buyer approves outgoing requests and the operations manager approves the sourcing decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Internal costs and supplier offers used different scopes, units and assumptions. Spreadsheet calculations were accessible, but maintaining comparable inputs took specialist work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable schemas and deterministic scenario calculations are straightforward to build. Bounded document extraction can reduce quote transcription while retaining source references.
tasks.still_hard: Avoidable costs differ from allocated costs. Capacity opportunity costs, supplier reliability, intellectual property and strategic dependence still require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the cheapest quoted option sacrifices scarce capacity, quality control or future flexibility.

ambition.what: A quarterly make-or-buy review of capacity-constrained components.

tasks.altitude: The estimator can test more demand and capacity scenarios and bring decision thresholds to planning meetings. They gain analytical scope; purchasing commitments and sourcing approval require existing delegated authority.

reach.task: Evaluate production equipment investment against outsourcing.
reach.learn: Discounted cash flow, avoidable cash costs and investment sensitivity.

reach.task: Assess supplier concentration exposure.
reach.learn: Disruption scenarios, exposure limits and mitigation costs.

evidence.claim: Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates, supporting deterministic rate comparison as an adjacent capability.
Make-or-buy scenario calculations and bounded quote extraction are proposed applications; the digest contains no direct make-or-buy case.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are unvalidated planning estimates.

assumptions: This baseline uses manufactured components; service and construction comparisons need different input templates.
Supplier waiting time is excluded from active task-time shares.
Internal cost and quote data can be compared at a defined quantity, quality and delivery scope.
No purchase order or supplier contract is created by the comparison tool.
unknowns: Are production routes, labour standards and capacity plans current?
Which overheads are avoidable for the decision horizon?
Who may request quotes and approve sourcing changes?
Are supplier documents permitted in an approved model-processing environment?
Does using labour data require employee consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Which quote formats can be handled with structured imports alone?
Which assumptions have most often reversed previous make-or-buy recommendations?
How should the calculator represent bottleneck capacity and minimum order quantities?
new_work: Review extracted exclusions and unusual commercial terms.
Maintain cost formulas, currency dates and scenario assumptions.
Refresh expired supplier quotes.
Compare realised costs with approved sourcing assumptions.
tasks.statement: Review material and labor requirements to decide whether it is more cost-effective to produce or purchase components.

tasks.short: Produce periodic project cost statements, explain variances and release approved reporting packs.

steps.what: Export posted project costs for the reporting period.
Collect open commitments, approved changes, progress and forecast updates.
Reconcile actuals, commitments, accruals and forecast against the approved budget.
Resolve missing postings, disputed accruals and unexplained project variances with cost owners.
Prepare cost statements, supporting schedules and variance commentary.

loop.input: Deterministically calculated report tables and source-linked explanations confirmed by cost owners.
loop.output: Short variance commentary attached to the generated cost statement.
loop.check: Validate every amount against the frozen dataset; require source references for explanations and controller approval before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per report; failed checks use factual templates and flag missing explanations.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations and formatting are deterministic. A bounded loop helps condense varied free-text explanations without inventing causes.

steps.what: Review material movements, unresolved exceptions and commentary; approve the report for release.
Distribute the approved report to the authorised internal recipients.
File the released report and its supporting evidence.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles period snapshots from the {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {PROJECT}, then generates statements in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions and controller approval; a bounded loop drafts source-linked commentary, and approved release automatically preserves the evidence pack and notifies recipients through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Period cut-offs, commitments and project updates were assembled from separate sources. Reusable report templates did not remove reconciliation and explanation work.
tasks.enabler_now: Validated imports, deterministic financial checks and document generation can cover the repeatable work. A small model loop can summarise confirmed explanations without calculating financial figures.
tasks.still_hard: Late costs, disputed progress, accrual estimates and optimistic forecasts cannot be resolved from transaction records alone.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge a plausible-looking forecast and identify when reported progress hides a likely cost overrun.

ambition.what: A weekly forecast-at-completion exception review for active projects.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends reporting time on exceptions and discussions with project owners. They can propose earlier forecast interventions; budget and report approval rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Update project forecasts from cost and progress movements.
reach.learn: Forecast drivers, contingency treatment and scenario comparison.

reach.task: Prepare and substantiate project accruals.
reach.learn: Cut-off rules, evidence standards and accrual reversals.

evidence.claim: Periodic financial statements can combine deterministic reconciliation, report generation and controlled release; no direct estimator reporting case is supplied.
The digest documents a report containing non-existent sources, supporting source checks for generated commentary.
Remaining effort and build ranges are planning hypotheses requiring validation over representative reporting periods.

assumptions: This baseline covers internal management reporting rather than contractual customer submissions.
Cost owners remain responsible for forecast and variance explanations.
Reports use frozen period snapshots and versioned mappings.
Separate manual archiving disappears because approved release creates the archive.
unknowns: Which statements are management reports and which have contractual or statutory requirements?
How are commitments relieved when invoices are posted?
Who approves accrual estimates and forecast changes?
Which report recipients and retention periods are authorised?
Do source feeds contain employee-level data requiring additional access or consultation controls under national rules?
research_questions: Can native reports supply reliable period snapshots and open commitments?
Which historical periods contain useful tests for late postings, reversals and duplicate commitments?
Can fixed commentary templates cover most reports without a model loop?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation failures and stale source feeds.
Review commentary against confirmed explanations.
Maintain report templates, thresholds and recipient lists.
Monitor releases, retained evidence and reporting revisions.
tasks.statement: Prepare cost and expenditure statements and other necessary documentation at regular intervals for the duration of the project.

tasks.short: Maintain a reliable directory of suppliers, contractors and subcontractors for estimating.

steps.what: Collect existing supplier records and recent supplier changes.
Request missing contact, capability and qualification information from suppliers.
Match supplier identities and reconcile duplicate or inconsistent directory entries.
Assess capability and qualification evidence; decide supplier eligibility for the directory.
Update supplier categories, contacts, evidence links and approved status in the directory.
Circulate directory copies to estimators and project teams.

tasks.design: Use the {PROCUREMENT} as the shared directory, with scheduled imports from the {ERP} and structured update requests through the {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic checks validate fields, match stable identifiers and queue ambiguous identities for review; a procurement specialist approves eligibility changes before publication. Teams use the live directory, removing circulated copies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier records serve different purposes across estimating and finance. Unclear field ownership and spreadsheet copies allow duplicates and stale qualifications to persist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing supplier records, forms and validation rules can handle most of the workflow. AI coding can make field mapping and exception screens cheaper to build; no model loop is necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Legal entity changes, disputed capabilities and inconsistent qualification evidence need investigation. A complete record does not establish supplier reliability.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish credible capabilities from unsupported claims and resolve supplier identities using commercial context.

ambition.what: A supplier-coverage gap review by trade and operating region for upcoming bids.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends less time copying contacts and chasing routine updates, and more time finding gaps in available suppliers. Procurement retains supplier eligibility and purchasing approval rights.

reach.task: Map qualified supplier coverage against the upcoming bid pipeline.
reach.learn: Category design, coverage measures and the distinction between missing evidence and missing supply.

evidence.claim: Supplier directories can use existing records applications, structured forms and deterministic validation.
Stable identifiers support automatic matching, while ambiguous identities and capability assessments need human review.

assumptions: The company maintains supplier master records in the {ERP} and a sourcing directory in the {PROCUREMENT}.
A spreadsheet currently reconciles records between systems and teams.
The directory supports estimating and does not authorize purchases or change payment details.
Routine information requests use approved templates and contact rules; people handle unusual replies.
Build ranges assume supported exports or interfaces and an existing supplier-record capability.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Consultation under national rules depends on whether employee data practices change.
unknowns: Which system owns each supplier field and who resolves conflicting updates.
Whether supplier identifiers remain consistent across the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}.
Whether the {PROCUREMENT} supports the required categories, access controls and approval states.
Which qualification checks are mandatory for each supplier category.
How many historical duplicates need manual cleanup.
Whether employee consultation is required under national rules; required consultation may extend the access range.
research_questions: Which directory fields materially improve supplier selection for estimates?
What proportion of duplicate candidates can be resolved using stable identifiers?
Can suppliers complete structured updates without creating extra support work?
new_work: Resolve identity conflicts and rejected updates.
Review qualification gaps and eligibility changes.
Maintain category definitions, validation rules and field ownership.
Monitor failed imports, unanswered requests and stale records.
Maintain contact-data access and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Prepare and maintain a directory of suppliers, contractors and subcontractors.

tasks.short: Establish cost codes, controls, reporting views and procedures for monitoring project costs.

steps.what: Agree reporting needs, cost ownership, thresholds and review frequency.
Document cost definitions, source fields, allocation rules and reporting responsibilities.
Reconcile sample transactions and commitments against project budgets using exports.
Configure cost views, refresh schedules, access and exception alerts.
Write operating procedures for refreshes, corrections, escalation and reporting.
Test sample periods, access restrictions, totals and alert behaviour.
Approve cost definitions, reporting controls and release readiness.
Activate approved reporting views and publish the operating procedure.

tasks.design: Configure project cost views in the {ERP} and {BI}, using a reusable mapping register in the {WORKFLOW} and validated imports from the {PROCUREMENT} and {PROJECT}. A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} checks totals and generates procedures from approved fields; release follows the financial controller's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost definitions differed across teams. Mapping, reconciliation and control documentation required repeated specialist effort even where reporting features already existed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration handles most reporting. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building import adapters, reconciliation checks and procedure templates; it does not settle accounting definitions.
tasks.still_hard: Allocating shared costs, distinguishing commitments from actuals and keeping historical comparisons consistent after code changes.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which cost signals justify intervention and negotiate definitions that project and finance teams can both use.

ambition.what: A reusable cost-monitoring starter package for small project teams.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends more time testing whether reports expose useful decisions and less time assembling reporting infrastructure. They can lead monitoring design; financial control approval remains with the financial controller.

reach.task: Define a governed project-cost dataset.
reach.learn: Data grain, refresh lineage, access controls and reconciliation tests.

reach.task: Reconcile project costs to the general ledger.
reach.learn: Accruals, allocation methods and period-close controls.

evidence.claim: Configured reporting, mapping registers and deterministic reconciliation are plausible building blocks; the digest provides no estimator-specific implementation case.
Build ranges and remaining-time estimates are planning hypotheses, not measured results.

assumptions: The baseline combines existing financial reports with manual mapping and control documentation.
The first release covers one project-cost model and a limited set of source feeds.
Time shares describe setup effort, not recurring report production.
The design needs no model loop when definitions and procedure fields are structured.
unknowns: Which reporting features and configuration rights are already available?
Are cost codes and project identifiers consistent across source systems?
Who can approve allocation rules and production configuration?
Will reporting expose individual employee costs or performance?
Which national consultation requirements and internal access reviews apply?
research_questions: Which native reporting features can replace custom development?
Which sample periods best reveal commitment duplication, late postings and allocation errors?
new_work: Maintain cost mappings and source-field contracts.
Investigate failed reconciliations and stale feeds.
Review access and reporting changes.
Update procedures when controls or responsibilities change.
tasks.statement: Set up cost monitoring and reporting systems and procedures.

tasks.short: Maintain the tender process, obtain comparable responses, negotiate terms and record approved agreements.

steps.what: Review tender rules, approval thresholds and standard commercial terms.
Approve changes to tender rules and commercial approval thresholds.
Set up the tender record, timetable, response fields and approval route.
Prepare the tender pack using scope documents and approved commercial templates.

loop.input: Approved scope, specification, response schema and locked commercial templates.
loop.output: Draft scope narrative and clarification questions within a deterministically assembled tender pack.
loop.check: Check required fields, source links and unchanged commercial clauses; the estimator checks scope coverage.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pack; missing scope or conflicting clauses block completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Project-specific scope prose needs synthesis; standard clauses and pack assembly use templates.

steps.what: Approve and issue the tender pack to shortlisted suppliers.
Log supplier responses and identify missing documents, qualifications and late submissions.

loop.input: Supplier responses and the tender's required response fields.
loop.output: Response register with source-linked qualifications and missing-document flags.
loop.check: Deterministic completeness and deadline checks; procurement reviews qualifications before using them.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per response; unreadable or ambiguous responses enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier qualifications arrive as inconsistent free text; structured response fields bypass the loop.

steps.what: Negotiate scope, price, delivery and risk allocation with suppliers.
Approve final commercial terms before committing to the supplier.
Copy tender correspondence and approved terms into a separate archive folder.

tasks.design: Configure tender records, deadlines, issuance approvals and retention in {PROCUREMENT}, linking approved terms in {CLM}. Templates assemble packs, while bounded loops draft scope prose and extract response qualifications; people negotiate and approve commitments. A complete tender record removes the separate duplicate archive.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tender rules, correspondence and commercial terms crossed departmental boundaries. Custom scope wording and supplier qualifications resisted simple templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing tender workflow features can handle routing and deadlines. Small text loops cover variable documents, and AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records.
tasks.still_hard: Fair treatment, negotiation strategy, contract deviations and supplier leverage require judgement. Formal tender procedures can constrain revisions and communications.
tasks.human_edge: The estimator knows which concessions preserve value and when a cheap offer transfers unacceptable risk.

ambition.what: A pre-negotiation briefing on scope exclusions and concession costs.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward supplier discussions and concession analysis as routing and filing shrink. Existing negotiating limits and commercial approval rights remain in place.

reach.task: Review tender integrity and conflicts of interest.
reach.learn: Evidence requirements, equal-treatment controls and escalation for procedural exceptions.

evidence.claim: Tender routing, deadlines, response registers and template assembly can use configured workflows and deterministic code.
The digest documents requisition-policy automation inside purchasing software; this is adjacent evidence, not proof of tender negotiation automation.
The proposed tender text loops and their review effort are design estimates, not documented estimator results.

assumptions: This task covers supplier and subcontractor tendering; customer-facing bid submission would need a different approval route.
Negotiations stay within an approved mandate; final commitments require commercial approval.
A separate archive can disappear only if the tender record meets retention and audit needs.
Time and build ranges are illustrative for one tender workflow; customer results may differ.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National rules govern consultation and any formal tender obligations.
unknowns: Does tendering mean buying from suppliers, bidding to customers, or both?
Which tender functions are already configured in the {PROCUREMENT}?
Who may issue tenders, negotiate concessions and make binding commitments?
Do formal tender requirements or separate archive obligations apply?
What access and employee consultation are required?
research_questions: Can the existing tender record retain correspondence and versioned terms without duplicate filing?
Can structured supplier response forms remove most qualification extraction?
Which contract deviations need specialist review before negotiations?
new_work: Review generated scope prose and extracted qualifications.
Maintain approval routes, response fields and commercial templates.
Handle failed submissions, late responses and retention exceptions.
Check that externally issued packs match the approved version.
tasks.statement: Establish and maintain tendering process, and conduct negotiations.

tasks.short: Study work methods and cost drivers to establish standard hours or identify cost reductions.

steps.what: Define the study question, process boundary, sampling method and success criteria.
Retrieve production, labour, quality and cost records for the selected process.
Observe work cycles and discuss delays, variation and practical constraints with workers.
Clean observations and separate setup, productive time, rework and abnormal interruptions.
Estimate standard hours and compare cost-reduction options with uncertainty and quality effects.
Run an authorised trial and check output, quality, safety and worker feedback.
Approve revised standards or cost changes after reviewing trial evidence and consultation outcomes.
Enter approved standard hours and costs with effective dates and supporting references.

tasks.design: A reusable study register in the {WORKFLOW} links structured observations with validated extracts from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}; deterministic analysis on the {DATA_PLATFORM} generates study tables and sensitivity results in the {DOCS}. People choose methods, interpret worker explanations and authorise trials and standards; approved changes update the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} with effective dates and evidence links.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each study needed a credible sampling design and local process knowledge. Data preparation and rebuilding calculations consumed time, but software could not establish whether observed work was representative.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable observation forms, import adapters and statistical scripts reduce setup and paperwork. No new inference breakthrough is required, and structured observations avoid a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Separate sustainable performance from unusual conditions, learning effects and measurement bias. Prove that apparent savings survive changes in product mix without harming quality or workers.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when a measured improvement transfers effort elsewhere, depends on unsustainable work intensity or excludes necessary work.

ambition.what: A post-change validation study that checks realised savings and sustainable standard hours.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends more time observing work, designing trials and checking whether savings persist. They can lead study design and challenge weak evidence; operational standards still need authorised approval.

reach.task: Design a controlled process-improvement trial.
reach.learn: Sampling, confounding, uncertainty intervals and causal inference.

reach.task: Translate validated process savings into a forecast.
reach.learn: Volume effects, implementation costs and the difference between released capacity and cash savings.

evidence.claim: Structured observation forms, repeatable calculations and controlled standard updates can support studies; the digest supplies no direct standard-hour study case.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; employee-data use and consultation requirements require assessment against the actual design and national rules.
Build ranges include an initial pilot but exclude long production cycles; remaining-time estimates are planning hypotheses.

assumptions: The study concerns process standards rather than individual worker ranking.
Observations use defined categories; people classify ambiguous interruptions.
Calculations flag unusual observations without automatically discarding them.
Existing trial authorisation and required employee consultation precede operational changes.
The access range allows initial consultation work; national procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Do standard hours affect pay, targets, staffing or individual evaluations?
What employee consultation, works-council involvement or agreements apply under national rules?
What GDPR lawful basis, retention period and assessment requirements apply to the intended observations?
Can study records use process-level or pseudonymised data?
Are sufficiently representative production cycles available during the pilot?
Who may authorise trials and approve standard changes?
research_questions: Which sampling method captures product mix, setup variation and learning effects?
Which existing standard calculations can be reused without custom development?
What follow-up period distinguishes sustained savings from temporary improvements?
new_work: Maintain observation categories and analytical methods.
Review data-quality flags and document inclusion decisions.
Keep consultation, trial and approval evidence.
Check realised savings and standard-hour drift after implementation.
Maintain effective dates and reverse superseded standards.
tasks.statement: Conduct special studies to develop and establish standard hour and related cost data or to reduce cost.

tasks.short: Inspect project sites and record conditions that affect cost estimates.

steps.what: Review plans and previous records; prepare a site inspection checklist.
Arrange site access, attendance and visit timing with the site contact.
Visit the site; record access, drainage, topography and visible utility conditions.
Confirm uncertain utility availability and access restrictions with responsible contacts.
Combine observations, photographs and confirmations into a draft site report.

loop.input: Recorded observations, photo references, confirmations and unresolved questions.
loop.output: A source-linked draft site report with explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Validate required sections and source references. Require support for each factual statement; retain contradictions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt. On validation failure, populate a template with original notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text observations need concise synthesis. Templates handle the report structure but cannot reliably summarize varied notes.

steps.what: Approve the site report and identify conditions requiring estimating allowances or specialist investigation.

tasks.design: A checklist generator uses approved templates and project references in the {DOCS}; configured scheduling in the {WORKFLOW} prepares visit arrangements. A mobile form in the {WORKFLOW} captures observations and photo references, while a bounded drafting loop prepares the report in the {DOCS}. The cost estimator approves the report and decides which uncertainties need allowances or specialist investigation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical conditions require a visit. Notes, photographs and confirmations also arrive separately, making report preparation awkward.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing mobile forms and document templates handle capture and assembly. AI coding can reduce implementation effort, and a bounded model loop can summarize recorded notes.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden services, ground conditions and utility capacity require reliable external evidence or specialist surveys. Software cannot establish these from photographs.
tasks.human_edge: Notice site conditions that the checklist misses, challenge assurances and judge when a specialist investigation is worth its cost.

ambition.what: Reassess site-risk allowances at design revisions using unresolved site questions.

tasks.altitude: Visits still dominate the work. Less report assembly leaves time to investigate expensive uncertainties; spending and bid approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate uncertain site conditions into contingency scenarios.
reach.learn: Scenario costing, contingency methods and how uncertainty affects the project budget.

evidence.claim: Site inspection depends on physical observation; structured capture can reduce paperwork without replacing the visit.
Templates and source-linked drafting can support report preparation; estimator-specific savings are not established by this digest.

assumptions: This task concerns construction or facilities projects within a mid-size European company.
The time shares describe a typical visit including local travel within the inspection step.
The estimate assumes existing document access and mobile forms; it excludes specialist survey equipment.
The solution records site conditions rather than monitoring employee performance.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Employee consultation depends on national rules and the actual deployment.
unknowns: Whether photography and mobile devices are permitted at project sites.
Which site records and utility confirmations are available before visits.
Whether the existing {WORKFLOW} supports offline capture.
Who can approve site-risk allowances and commission specialist surveys.
Whether national rules or employee agreements require consultation; any required consultation may extend the access range.
research_questions: Which missing observations have caused costly estimate revisions?
Can checklist-based reports preserve the detail needed by downstream estimators?
How reliably does the drafting loop preserve uncertainty and conflicting observations?
new_work: Review drafted reports against original observations.
Maintain inspection templates and required evidence fields.
Resolve incomplete uploads and broken photo references.
Maintain access, retention settings and drafting validation rules.
tasks.statement: Visit site and record information about access, drainage and topography, and availability of utility services.

tasks.short: Build a reusable historical cost base and select credible comparators for new estimates.

steps.what: Retrieve historical actual costs and project cost codes.
Find archived estimates, quantities and explanations of unusual costs.

loop.input: Archived estimates and project closeout notes for selected projects.
loop.output: Historical context register with quantities, scope differences and exceptional costs linked to sources.
loop.check: Validate project identifiers and source references; estimator checks quantities and exceptions before reuse.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per project; unsupported entries remain missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations of one-off costs and scope differences are embedded in varied narrative documents.

steps.what: Map cost codes and normalise units, currency and price dates.
Judge comparability and exclude misleading records or unsupported adjustments.
Publish the selected costs and their limitations for future estimates.

tasks.design: Load historical costs from {ERP} into {DATA_PLATFORM}, apply approved mappings and normalisation rules, and quarantine incomplete records. A bounded loop extracts context from {DOCS}; the estimator selects valid comparators and publishes them in a configured {WORKFLOW} records app with provenance and limitations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Historical records used inconsistent codes and lacked the context needed to distinguish repeatable costs from one-off events.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic data pipelines can handle mapping and normalisation. Faster coding lowers connector costs, while bounded extraction makes archived narrative context easier to recover.
tasks.still_hard: Missing quantities, changed accounting treatment and different delivery conditions can make apparently similar projects incomparable.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when an attractive historical unit cost describes a fundamentally different job.

ambition.what: Give product development teams qualified cost ranges before detailed designs exist.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends less time searching archives and repairing formats, and more time qualifying comparable work. They can accept or exclude comparators within an agreed method; budget approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Define a reusable cost dataset with traceable measures.
reach.learn: Data grain, lineage, slowly changing mappings and validation rules.

reach.task: Reconcile historical project costs to posted accounting records.
reach.learn: Accruals, reversals, allocation changes and period closure.

evidence.claim: Cost collection, code mapping and normalisation are established deterministic data-processing patterns.
Historical comparability needs domain judgement even when records are structured.

assumptions: Initial scope covers one cost taxonomy and a bounded archive.
Normalisation uses approved exchange rates and price indices; missing values are not invented.
Published records retain original values, adjustment methods and source dates.
Labour data is aggregated where possible. GDPR applies to identifiable records; assess EU AI Act duties and national consultation rules if employee monitoring changes.
unknowns: Historical coverage, archive quality and rights to reuse supplier prices.
Availability of delivered quantities and final scope records.
Changes in cost codes, overhead allocation and accounting policies.
Whether comparator selection authority can be delegated to the estimator.
research_questions: Which fields most strongly determine comparability for the selected product or project family?
Can existing reporting exports supply the required data before building new interfaces?
new_work: Resolve quarantined records and missing context.
Maintain cost mappings, indices and source permissions.
Review ageing comparators and retire misleading benchmarks.
Monitor reconciliation totals and data refresh failures.
tasks.statement: Collect historical cost data to estimate costs for current or future products.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts towards scope interpretation, comparator quality, uncertainty and early cost interventions. Formal commercial and spending approval rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Budget analysts: turn qualified estimates into phased budgets and rolling forecasts.
Accountants: reconcile cost evidence and explain accounting effects.
Business intelligence analysts: maintain traceable cost measures and exception reporting.
Financial managers: assess margin and cash consequences of delivery alternatives.
skills_to_grow: Cost taxonomy and data reconciliation
Source checking and document version control
Scenario analysis and uncertainty communication
Progress measurement and remaining-cost forecasting
Commercial negotiation and change control
Validation of bounded model outputs
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a cost-options advisory service from early design through delivery, using qualified historical evidence and current project costs to make uncertainty visible before commitments are made.

role_batches.altitude: The estimator moves from assembling documents and calculation sheets toward testing scope, supplier and scheduling choices. Commercial commitments and project baselines retain their existing approval owners; additional authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Budget analyst: connect project estimates to phased forecasts.
Accountant: reconcile estimated costs with comparable actuals.
Financial risk specialist: assess supplier and scope exposure.
Business intelligence analyst: measure assumption accuracy over completed work.
skills_to_grow: Design common scope and cost-line schemas.
Validate deterministic cost models and source-linked document extraction.
Explain uncertainty and sensitivity without false precision.
Learn commercial approval limits and contract risk allocation.
Use actual outcomes to improve productivity and contingency assumptions.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide an early cost-options service that compares supplier substitutions and practical sequencing choices before scope is committed, then refresh those options as costs and capacity change.

role_batches.altitude: The cost estimator becomes a stronger designer of cost evidence and decision scenarios. Their week shifts toward assumptions, operational discussions and validation; pricing, sourcing, budget and employment-related decisions retain their assigned approvers.
reach: Cost reconciliation and accrual evidence with accountants.
Governed cost datasets with business intelligence analysts.
Controlled cost-reduction trials with data scientists.
skills_to_grow: Data mapping and financial reconciliation.
Avoidable-cost and capacity modelling.
Sampling, experimental design and uncertainty.
Configuration, import validation and change control.
Source checking for bounded document extraction and drafting.
Employee-data handling and consultation under applicable national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a reusable cost-decision service that connects estimates, actual costs, sourcing scenarios and verified savings. Start with approved file imports and templates, then add integrations where access and repeat use justify them.

role_batches.altitude: Physical inspection and commercial judgement remain central. The estimator gains time for site uncertainty and supplier coverage analysis; bid, purchasing and spending authority do not automatically expand.
reach: Budget analysts: connect site uncertainty to contingency scenarios.
Business intelligence analysts: connect supplier coverage to upcoming bids.
skills_to_grow: Structured evidence capture and source checking.
Contingency and scenario costing.
Supplier data quality and entity matching.
Coverage analysis and exception handling.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide an early bid-readiness review combining unresolved site risks, contingency scenarios and supplier coverage gaps.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
